results.title: Five Key Trends Shaping Biopharma and Biotech in 2025
results.content: As clinical trials grow increasingly complex, predicting timelines, managing costs and ensuring success have become formidable challenges for biopharma companies. These insights are fueling innovation: Over half of surveyed sponsors across all company sizes highlighted innovative trial designs as the top trend transforming the industry and the top innovative strategy they’re currently pursuing. By investing in therapeutic areas with high patient demand and significant innovation potential, biopharma companies are accelerating the development of life-changing treatments. Biopharma companies are increasingly looking to emerging markets as key regions for clinical trials, driven by evolving regulatory standards and the promise of faster, more efficient trial processes. These changes enable biopharma companies to navigate complex requirements more efficiently, accelerating access to diverse patient populations and addressing the regulatory hurdles that often delay trial progress. Strategic investments in high-impact therapeutic areas, the integration of AI into clinical processes and the expansion of trials into emerging markets are reshaping drug development.

results.title: Pharmaceutical industry trends 2025, outlook and strategies
results.content: By Bill Coyle,  Rahul Pathak,  Raluca Cenusa,  and Divyata Manvati. ### Pharma priority No. 2: Accelerating R&D with data, AI and patient-centric trials. Pharma companies are investing heavily in data and AI to foster innovation and reduce drug development costs and timelines, with 85% of biopharma executives said they planned to invest in data, digital and AI in R&D for 2025. Pharma companies are optimizing their supply chains and building resilience using technology, especially AI. Nearly every pharma company expects to invest in data, digital and AI for commercial and medical operations in the near future. There’s been much talk of pharma’s trust deficit with healthcare consumers, but our Future of Health Report reveals that consumers are open to pharma-driven digital patient engagement to improve care. No wonder seven of the top-12 pharma companies announced digital investments in patient support between 2023 and 2024.
